_doc: Written by adapters/godot_controller.py from the project's resources; regenerate when the controller is retuned. Every key is documented in templates/controller.json. knobs: value, group, source, unit, hands. model: what the arithmetic expects from the knobs, for the measurement to be compared with.

run_speed.hands: how fast the ground goes by; every horizontal reach scales with it (a running jump is run_speed x airtime). Raise it and every gap in the district gets easier.

ground_acceleration.hands: how long the first step takes: run_speed / this is the seconds to top speed. Under 0.1 s reads as instant, over 0.25 s reads as skating.

ground_deceleration.hands: how far a released stick slides: run_speed^2 / (2 x this) is the stopping distance. Also the rate a hurt knockback bleeds off at.

air_acceleration.hands: how much the stick steers a jump; low values make a jump a commitment, high values make every gap forgiving.

air_deceleration.hands: how much a jump keeps its speed when the stick is let go; low values carry, high values drop.

turn_acceleration.hands: the reversal: run_speed / this is the seconds a turn takes to cross zero. The design asks for instant; a value several times the ground acceleration keeps a turn a turn without a snap.

jump_height.hands: the ceiling of a full hold; a ledge higher than this with no facing wall is a wall. Changing it re-judges every ledge in the district.

jump_time_to_apex.hands: the snap: short is springy, long is floaty. With the height fixed, gravity falls out of it; the airtime and so every horizontal reach follow.

fall_gravity_multiplier.hands: the fall against the rise; above 1 the fall is quicker and the jump lands with weight. 1.0 is a symmetric, floaty arc. The single biggest feel knob.

jump_cut_multiplier.hands: how much of the rise a released button keeps; low values make a tap a hop, 1.0 removes variable height.

max_fall_speed.hands: terminal velocity: how a long drop ends. Low values float down, high values hit the floor.

coyote_time.hands: the grace after walking off a ledge in which a jump still fires; 0.08 to 0.12 s is felt as forgiveness, more is felt as a double jump.

jump_buffer_time.hands: how early a jump can be pressed before landing and still fire; 0.1 to 0.2 s. Also the window a jump pressed during a dash waits in.

dash_distance.hands: how far one dash goes with altitude held; a gap the run cannot cross and the dash can is one dash wide.

dash_duration.hands: the commitment: how long the dash cannot be steered. Under 0.12 s it is a step, over 0.25 s it is a cutscene. A duration not a whole number of frames runs to the next frame.

dash_cooldown.hands: the wait before the next ground dash; short makes dashing a way of running.

dash_grants_iframes.hands: whether the dash is a dodge; on, every attack can be dashed through and enemies must be designed for it.

dash_iframe_time.hands: how much of the dash is invulnerable when it is a dodge.

can_dash_in_air.hands: whether the dash exists in the air at all (possession is a flag elsewhere); on, a jump plus a dash is the widest gap.

wall_slide_speed.hands: how fast a wall is slid down; slow makes a wall a place to think, fast makes it a fall with friction.

wall_jump_push.hands: the kick away from the wall; with the lockout it is how far the kick carries before the stick takes over, and so the widest shaft.

wall_jump_height.hands: the height each kick gains; a shaft is climbed at this per kick.

wall_stick_time.hands: how long the wall keeps the player after the stick lets go, so a turn-and-jump does not drop them.

wall_jump_lockout_time.hands: how long the kick owns the stick; too short and a stick held toward the wall cancels the kick, too long and the jump cannot be steered.

same_wall_lockout_scale.hands: how much of the kick's flight the wall just left refuses; at 1.0 a single wall cannot be climbed, below it a single wall is a slow ladder.

same_wall_lockout_margin.hands: the extra refusal on top of the scaled flight.

hitstop_light_frames.hands: the freeze on an ordinary hit; 2 to 3 frames reads as contact, more reads as lag.

hitstop_heavy_frames.hands: the freeze on a heavy hit; the difference from the light one is what makes weight.

hitstop_heavy_threshold.hands: the damage at which a hit is heavy.

hitstop_max_seconds.hands: the longest any freeze can hold, so a stack of hits cannot become a slideshow.

flinch_knockback_mult.hands: the share of knockback an enemy that flinches (not staggered) takes.

player_hurt_knockback.hands: the speed the player is pushed at when hit; with the ground deceleration it is how many frames of control a hit costs.

player_iframe_time.hands: how long after a hit the player cannot be hit again; the breathing room a mistake buys.

iframe_flash_hz.hands: how fast the invulnerable flash blinks.

contact_damage_mult.hands: the share of an enemy's power a touch deals.

stat_max_bonus.hands: the stat curve's ceiling (the systems-designer's number; read here, tuned there).

stat_half_point.hands: the stat curve's half point (the systems-designer's number; read here, tuned there).
